title: Low-degree projection bound above the second moment
statement: For every real $q\ge 2$, there is a constant $C\ge 1$ such that, if $q=4$, then $C=5\sqrt{3}$. For every finite product probability space $P$ with $n$ coordinates, every real-valued function $f$ on its outcome space, and every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, the degree-at-most-$k$ projection satisfies $\|f^{\le k}\|_{q,P}\le C^k\|f\|_{q,P}$.
hypotheses_covered: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite product probability space $P$ with $n$ coordinates
A real-valued function $f$ on the outcome space
replaced: For every $q\ge2$ there exists $C\ge1$, with $C=5\sqrt3$ if $q=4$, such that for every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, every $k\in\mathbb N$, and every real $f$ on its outcome space, $\|f^{\le k}\|_{q,P}\le C^k\|f\|_{q,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $h^{\le k}=\sum_{|S|\le k}h_S$.
